speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Heading: on contragredient Lie algebras
summary: Only a dated heading and the title \ru{О контраградиентных алгебрах Ли} survive before the next dated heading, 21 September, on P000981. The catalog range extends into P000982, but those mathematical notes belong to the following meeting. No mathematical claim is assigned to this heading-only record.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Reading list and finite-dimensional Lie theory
summary: The meeting begins with a reading list on highest-weight modules and Kac--Moody algebras. Macdonald's June 1981 Bourbaki lecture can be identified exactly as expos\'e 577, \emph{Affine Lie algebras and modular forms}; Humphreys' contribution is the 1980 LNM 831 chapter, pp.~72--103 \citep{macdonald1981affine,humphreys1980highest}. The intervening exposition, explicitly marked I.~M.~G., reviews roots, the Weyl group, Chevalley--Serre relations, highest weights and characters. A speculative Lorentz/neutrino aside has insufficient mathematical specification. The content ends at Rudakov's heading on P000984, not at the catalog endpoint. Several mistakes are in the notebook itself: the order of the symmetric group, the root/weight lattice distinction and omitted off-diagonal restrictions.

speaker: A. N. Rudakov
title: Contragredient Lie algebras and Cartan-matrix types
summary: Rudakov starts on P000984 with generators, relations, an enlarged Cartan space and a maximal ideal avoiding that space. He then removes redundant central directions and states the finite/affine/indefinite trichotomy for indecomposable generalized Cartan matrices. The literal affine alternative is internally contradictory. At the top of P000986 Gelfand adds the two Rogers--Ramanujan identities. The arrow returning to S.~I.~Gelfand on that page marks the next record. The historical construction should be compared with \citet[Chapter II]{kac1968graded} and \citet[\S2]{macdonald1981affine}; the latter's Serre-presentation convention must not silently replace the maximal-ideal definition for nonsymmetrizable matrices.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Verma embeddings and a root-multiplicity question
summary: The return arrow on P000986 begins a review of Verma modules and the Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand criterion for embeddings. The formulas mix the notebook's unshifted highest weight with a negative rho shift and do not delimit the finite-dimensional semisimple scope of the quoted theorem. At the top of P000987, Gelfand asks for root-space dimensions and independent words for general Cartan matrices. The next dated heading starts Seifert's talk. The multiplicity question is indexed, but neither efficiency nor a uniform positive combinatorial formula is demanded in the surviving wording; no artificial open conjecture is extracted.

speaker: Benedict Seifert
title: Transformation-group geometry and a Bruhat-type decomposition
summary: The actual heading is on P000987 and includes a question mark after the Russian surname and the affiliation Paris. Fixed sets of pointwise stabilizers define a closure geometry; the speaker builds flags, proposes four axioms and asserts a double-coset decomposition. The closest publication is Seifert's \emph{Transitivity Properties, Bruhat Decomposition and Tits Systems for Transformation Groups}, received 5 March 1983, published June 1984. Its exact axiom list could not be read in this run, so the identification is partial. Seifert's later paper explicitly distinguishes its new tree transitivity and proof from the earlier work \citep[Introduction and reference S.1]{seifert1986highly}. Gelfand's three concrete double-coset exercises occur on P000989 before the Zelevinsky heading.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Equioriented type-A quiver orbits and their geometry
summary: The actual exposition begins in the lower part of P000989 and explicitly reports \citet{abeasisdelfrakraft1981geometry}, whose September 1981 issue and receipt date of 1 April 1981 precede the meeting. It explains the finite orbit classification, rank invariants, good singularities of orbit closures and the determinantal special case. The closing analogy with Schubert geometry has a precise later realization in Zelevinsky's 1985 paper; the accompanying p-adic multiplicity connection must be distinguished from that purely geometric identification. The next dated heading on P000990 begins Kirillov's talk.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Rank-two Serre presentations, free Lie dimensions and interlacing arrays
summary: Kirillov asks about the two-generator Lie algebra with two Serre relations, gives the multigraded Witt formula before relations, identifies a Catalan specialization, and passes to the enveloping algebra and a Hilbert-series logarithm. A bare lexicographic word list does not specify a reduction algorithm. Gelfand then asks for the number of integer interlacing arrays with four fixed top entries. The latter counts a basis of one irreducible representation, not distinct representations of that highest weight. The record ends on P000991; the next meeting starts on P000992.

speaker: A. S. Schwarz
title: Supergravity as the geometry of a real supersurface
summary: Schwarz treats real \((4|4)\)-dimensional supersurfaces in \(\mathbb C^{4|2}\), a holomorphic volume-preserving pseudogroup, the odd complex tangent distribution and its Levi form. The action is written as a delta-function surface integral; a preliminary exponent on P000993 is explicitly replaced by the Jacobian-corrected expression on P000994. An SCR structure retains a determinant normalization absent from ordinary CR data. The October 1981 announcement is identified bibliographically, and the detailed formulas are verified in \citet[\S3, pp.~44--48]{schwarz1982supergravity}, received 15 February 1982. The broader field-space-democracy work is not confused with this exact Levi determinant formula. The record ends before the 23 November heading on P000995.
